Issued at 214 PM CDT Sun Sep 13 2026

Our attention turns to late tonight through Monday where confidence 
is high on widespread rain across the CWA. Model ensembles are 
pretty consistent on the large closed low aloft tracking eastward 
across the Northern Plains/Canada through the day and deepening 
before tracking northeastward into Manitoba/Ontario Monday 
night/Tuesday. A jet streak (~50kts) on the PVA/southeastern side of 
this low will provide lift across the region with speeds at 250mb at 
70+kts aiding in divergence aloft. At the surface, the low/cold 
front will be over the western Dakotas/MT/WY 12Z Monday with the 
front tracking swiftly eastward, exiting our far eastern CWA by 
early Monday evening. Ahead of the cold front within the warm 
sector, ample amounts of warm air and low level moisture is forecast 
per south to slight southeast winds with 850mb temps between 12 to 
15C and dewpoints at this level as high as 15C. Dewpoints at the 
surface will rise into the mid 50s to mid 60s (highest east of the 
James River) per surface winds out of the south/southeast. The leads 
to strong IVT transport from the gulf with PWAT values still 
forecast between 1.5 to 1.75" which is well over the 90th percentile 
for this time of year per with NAEFs still indicating these values 
about 3 standard deviations above climo!

So with this setup, models are also consistent on this WAA rain 
moving in from the west/southwest and over central SD around ~06Z 
where it will track and become widespread across the CWA by 12Z. 
Several CAMS indicate an additional line or cluster of heavier 
rain/storms developing over southern to southeastern SD per better 
forcing and moisture. This looks to clip and/or merge with the 
ongoing widespread rain over east central SD/MN potentially 
leading to higher QPF here. Behind the front/drier air, rain 
will diminish west to east across the CWA with the rain exiting
central SD by the midday/early afternoon and exiting eastern 
SD/western MN by late afternoon. If the low slows down, then 
rain will move in and exit the area later. Confidence remains 
high as NBM pops range from 80-100% over the CWA.

06Z run of EC/Canadian ensembles overall indicate 24 hr QPF totals 
between 0.3 to 0.8" with the higher QPF over northeastern SD/MN per 
Canadian and more east central SD per EC. GEFS is still running 
lower on overall totals with mean around 0.3". Latest NBM 
deterministic QPF matches up well with the Canadian and ENS with
highest amounts east of the James River. However, HREF and NBM 
5.2 does run a bit higher in totals, with a potential for rain 
in excess of an inch east of the James River. Therefore, 
NBM(5.0) probability of a half inch is 50-90% widespread over 
the CWA and 1" is 55-60% over east central SD through west 
central MN. 2" or more is 15-20% over portions of Big Stone 
County in MN. 90th percentile (10% chance) has values of 1-2". 
EC EFI range from 0.5 to 0.7 and no shift of tails meaning most 
EC members are near reforecast climatology therefore nothing 
anomalous forecasted. However, as the previous shift mentioned, 
the warmer air will lead to a large warm cloud layer (11-12K 
feet) that is an ingredient for flash flooding along with this 
excess moisture expected. WPC ERO does highlight a marginal 
risk (15%) mainly Coteau and eastward per this better 
moisture/QPF and deepening low. Storm motion is forecast to be 
about 20kts so not overly fast but not too slow either which 
should help keep flooding to a minimum along with soils being 
able to handle the moisture. However, any training/backbuilding 
(especially Coteau/eastward) may result in localized flooding. 
Lastly, CAPE will be at most 500-800j/kg over portions of south 
central to east central SD with shear of 50kts across the CWA. 
With lack of strong vertical growth aloft, no severe weather 
anticipated, however, weak thunderstorms will be possible with 
the rain.

Lastly, winds will be on the increase across central SD per 
steepening pressure gradient between the exiting high and incoming 
low with gusts up to 30kts along and west of the Mo River. Adding in 
the LLJ and these gusty winds will spread eastward with gusts of 25-
40 kts across the CWA by 12Z Monday. Behind the front per CAA and 
weak pressure rises (CAA strongest over north central SD 18Z) winds 
will turn westerly to northwesterly Monday afternoon through Monday 
evening with gusts increasing between 30 to potentially 45kts across 
the CWA, with highest gusts over Corson/Dewey. NBM is bit bullish on 
winds compared to HREF with models indicating the better CAA right 
behind the front not coinciding with the higher pressure rises,
which occur more Monday night. Also the CAA becomes weaker as 
it tracks east. Anyways, winds will remain gusty (20-35kts) through
the night before diminishing through Tuesday as low exits the 
region and high moves in. Therefore with collab, issued a Wind 
Advisory for Corson and Dewey valid 17Z Monday to 0
